newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Third former S.Korean president to appear in court.
newsitem.headline: Third former S.Korean president to appear in court.

text.p: In a dramatic twist to the appeals trial of convicted former South Korean presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo, the high court said on Monday it would force a third former head of state to appear.
The prospect of three former presidents appearing in the same courtroom has added theatrical suspense to the appeals by Chun and Roh.

But Choi Kyu-hah, a caretaker president between the assassination of presidential strongman Park Chung-hee in 1979 and Chun's violent grab for power, has stubbornly refused to heed previous court orders to show up as a witness.
On Monday, his lawyer Lee Ki-Chang remained defiant. "Even if he is forced to take the stand, he would not testify," Lee told reporters.
Chun was sentenced to death in August for mutiny and treason in connection with a December 1979 coup and a massacre of pro- democracy demonstrators in May the following year.
He was also convicted of bribery for amassing hundreds of millions of dollars while in office.
Roh was sentenced to 22-1/2 years in jail on similar charges.
"We have decided to force ex-president Choi to testify at the next trial because he had repeatedly refused to comply with our summons," said the court official, who declined to be named.
The next hearing is on Thursday.
Choi stepped down in August 1980 shortly before then army general Chun took office.
The court wants him to explain the events surrounding Chun's rise to the presidential Blue House.
Prosecutors have said Chun forced Choi from office as part of the putsch. Chun maintains Choi asked him to step in to save the country from unrest.
Choi has maintained that standing as a witness would set a bad precedent for future presidents.
Two opposition parties applauded the court's decision.
"We welcome the court's morally right choice," the main opposition National Congress for New Politics said in a statement.
"Choi must reveal the truth to the public by testifying at court. Choi should remember that the public is watching closely. We urge him to reveal every detail regarding the coup and the massacre."
The Democratic Party released a statement saying it hoped Choi's testimony would help "put history to rights".
But the United Liberal Democratic Party said "this is a lamentable occasion where one former president has to be forced to stand in the court that is trying two other former presidents".
Fourteen former aides to Chun and Roh are also fighting convictions in the appeals case.
